assets.purpose: canonical U-shaped geometry, material, clinical-window and biophilic-identity goalpost
assets.prompt:
Create one photorealistic architectural reference image for a buildable contemporary MASS-TIMBER BIOPHILIC HOSPITAL, shown in a clean front-left three-quarter view at human eye level with a mild elevated perspective, 16:9 landscape. This is the canonical geometry and material goalpost for a precise modular 3D model, so make every floor, bay, opening, wing, terrace and roof junction legible and internally consistent.

Use a restrained four-storey U-shaped hospital approximately 70 metres wide by 50 metres deep. Two occupied patient-room wings frame a landscaped healing courtyard that opens toward the viewer. Join the wings at the rear with a clinical bar, and bridge the courtyard entrance with a dramatic transparent triple-height public atrium whose warm exposed glulam tree columns and CLT floor edges are visible through real low-iron glass. The atrium and entry canopy must be integrated into the hospital structure, not a glass box tacked onto the facade. Provide a recessed public entrance at courtyard grade beneath a deep honey-glulam canopy, accessible drop-off lane and calm stone-paved forecourt. A separate ambulance/service bay should be only a subtle hint on the far right side, not competing with the public entry.

Patient wings: three upper clinical floors above a taller transparent/charred-timber public podium. Use a rigorous hospital bay cadence: broad paired patient-room windows at every structural bay, deeply recessed behind honey-toned vertical timber fins and warm timber rainscreen piers. Each window is layered physical low-E glass with dark thermal-break frame, operable vent, pale curtain and restrained occupied care-room depth. Alternate a few open timber-screened loggias and planted patient terraces, but keep the facade calm, regular and clinical rather than residential. Show exposed glulam columns and CLT slab edges at the atrium, canopy, colonnade and terrace structure. Use charred black timber only at the robust ground-floor service/public base and selected cores.

Biophilic identity: living green-wall panels climb selected solid bays on both courtyard wings and wrap the atrium edges; integrated planter ledges with grasses and trailing vines mark each floor; the courtyard contains small deciduous trees, therapeutic planting beds, benches and a shallow rain garden. Vegetation must be architecturally integrated and maintained, never a jungle hiding the building.

Roof: flat green roofs with gravel fire breaks and realistic parapet depth; a large photovoltaic canopy floats on a precise dark steel/glulam grid over the rear clinical bar and shades a fourth-floor healing terrace. Include two screened mechanical penthouses, a few skylights, roof drains and narrow service paths. The PV canopy must read as buildable roof infrastructure, not decorative blue glass.

Materials: honey-coloured exposed glulam/CLT; fine vertical timber rainscreen; restrained shou-sugi-ban charcoal base; pale local stone/concrete plinth and paving; dark bronze-black thermally broken frames; neutral high-transmission low-E glazing; vivid but plausible planting. Use soft clear late-afternoon daylight, crisp natural shadows, high-end architectural photography, 35mm lens, physically correct PBR response and detailed construction joints, returns, soffits, flashings, gutters and interior depth.

Avoid: generic rectangular hospital box, cartoon, illustration, stylized CGI, toy or LEGO studs, sci-fi curves, all-glass office building, residential balconies, blank blue/black windows, flat printed interiors, excessive vegetation hiding openings, random bay cadence, extra wings, impossible cantilevers, detached atrium, floating canopy, readable text, logos, watermarks or people blocking the architecture.

assets.purpose: rectified public elevation, patient-window cadence and atrium registration
assets.prompt:
Using the supplied canonical mass-timber biophilic hospital as the exact design source, create a photorealistic ORTHOGRAPHIC FRONT ELEVATION of the SAME building. Preserve the same four principal storeys, 70-metre-wide U-shaped composition, two patient-room wings, open healing courtyard, central triple-height glass atrium, integrated honey-glulam entry canopy, dark charred-timber public podium, deep timber patient-room bays, vertical green-wall strips, roof gardens, two black screened mechanical penthouses and the photovoltaic canopy over the rear clinical bar.

Camera: centered square-on to the public front, perfect vertical and horizontal rectification, no converging lines, minimal lens distortion, the full building from left edge to right edge and ground to roof visible against a pale neutral sky with only a narrow forecourt strip. This is a registration source, not a redesign.

Make the facade construction unambiguous. On each wing, retain exactly three upper patient-room rows above the taller ground-floor podium. Use repeated paired dark-framed low-E windows with pale curtains and restrained occupied room depth. Keep the timber columns, beams, CLT slab/fascia edges, recessed planter troughs, vertical fins and living-wall bands aligned to the same floor datums. The atrium glazing must expose the same glulam tree columns, bridges and circulation depth. Keep the entry canopy broad, shallow and structurally supported, centered on the atrium. Materials must remain honey timber, charred black timber, neutral clear glass, pale stone/concrete and controlled planting.

Render as high-end architectural survey photography with even neutral daylight, crisp PBR material response and construction joints. Do not change floor count, bay cadence, wing width, atrium width, canopy position, roof silhouette or material zoning. Do not add text, signage, people, vehicles, unrelated buildings, perspective drama, cartoon styling, fake printed windows, blue opaque glass, extra balconies or additional wings.

assets.purpose: U-shaped plan, open healing courtyard, roof infrastructure and service-separation registration
assets.prompt:
Create a photorealistic HIGH OBLIQUE AERIAL / ROOF reference of the exact same mass-timber biophilic hospital in the supplied canonical and front-elevation images. Preserve its exact four-storey identity and front composition: two patient-room wings forming a U-shaped plan open toward the public forecourt, central integrated triple-height glass atrium and honey-glulam entrance canopy, charred-timber ground-floor plinth, deep timber window bays, vertical green-wall strips, planted ledges, black mechanical screens and photovoltaic canopy.

Reveal a plausible 70 by 50 metre plan. The two front wings must extend back and connect through one broad rear clinical bar around a clearly open landscaped healing courtyard; do not fill the courtyard with a solid building. The central public atrium should span the rear of the courtyard and its glazed roof/vertical enclosure must connect continuously to the two wings. Show therapeutic paths, benches, low planting beds, one rain garden and several small trees inside the courtyard. The entrance canopy projects toward the front drop-off and is supported by the same glulam structural language.

Make the roof a precise construction source: extensive sedum/meadow roofs on both patient wings and the rear bar, dark metal parapet flashings, continuous gravel fire breaks, narrow maintenance paths, roof drains and scuppers, several rectangular skylights, two screened mechanical penthouses set back from the public edges, and one large orderly photovoltaic canopy on a dark steel/glulam rack over the rear clinical bar/healing terrace. The PV modules must show credible rows, gaps, frame depth and support columns. Include a separate ambulance bay and service court at the far rear-right with a deep timber/black-metal canopy, two emergency doors and screened loading/mechanical functions, visually separated from the public arrival.

Camera from front-left about 35 degrees downward, complete roof and all exterior edges visible, 16:9 landscape, high-end architectural photography, realistic PBR materials and shadows. Do not redesign the facade, change floor count or bay cadence, add extra wings, close the courtyard, move the public entrance, create a blue-glass office building, add helipad markings, cover roofs with random equipment, use cartoon styling, labels or watermarks.

assets.purpose: rear clinical elevation, two-bay ambulance arrival and service construction registration
assets.prompt:
Create a photorealistic REAR-RIGHT THREE-QUARTER architectural reference of the exact same mass-timber biophilic hospital shown in the supplied canonical front and aerial views. Preserve the 70 x 50 metre U-shaped four-storey hospital, two patient wings, rear connecting clinical bar, honey timber facade grid, charred public/service plinth, living-wall strips, planted ledges, extensive green roof, photovoltaic canopy and screened rooftop plant.

The rear and right side must logically complete this same healthcare building. Show the rear clinical bar as an occupied hospital wing with a disciplined grid of deep paired clinical windows, warm timber rainscreen piers and occasional dark charred service bays. At the rear-right, create a clearly separate but architecturally integrated emergency/ambulance arrival: a deep glulam-and-dark-metal canopy supported by real columns; exactly two ambulance bays/doors with one correctly scaled ambulance partly under the canopy; red emergency-route paving stripe without readable words; recessed staff entrance; stretcher vestibule; service doors; oxygen/utility cabinets; trench drain; bollards and screened loading/mechanical yard. It should read operational, clean and calm, not industrial or theatrical.

Continue the patient-room bay cadence around the right side with real deep reveals, timber fins, dark thermally broken frames, neutral low-E glass, pale curtains and restrained occupied interior depth. Continue CLT slab edges, planters, downpipes and wall bases through the corners. Show the courtyard only as a glimpse through the side/atrium connection, confirming it remains open. Roof construction must match the aerial: meadow green roof, gravel fire breaks, parapets, skylights, two black screened penthouses and one large PV canopy on a precise frame over the rear terrace.

Camera squarely reveals rear and right side, 16:9 landscape, neutral late-afternoon architectural photography, realistic PBR materials, crisp joints, flashing, weathering and glazing depth. Do not add extra floors, a helipad, a third ambulance bay, blue opaque office glass, random balconies, generic concrete facade, a detached service shed, cartoon styling, labels, text or watermarks.

assets.purpose: custom timber, glulam, charred timber, mineral, living-wall and photovoltaic PBR sources
patient-room low-e glazing and public-atrium occupied-depth registration
assets.prompt:
Create a photorealistic two-panel WINDOW, ATRIUM AND OCCUPIED-DEPTH construction reference for the exact same mass-timber biophilic hospital. Split the image vertically into two equal panels with a thin neutral divider and no labels or typography.

LEFT PANEL: a square-on close view of one complete typical upper patient-room bay from the supplied hospital. Show the full honey-glulam/timber frame from one structural pier to the next, deep timber-clad jambs and soffit, a paired dark thermally broken window system, separate neutral low-E panes with subtle blue-grey sky/tree reflections, operable vents, gaskets, black sill flashing and restrained clear transmission. Behind the glass, set at least 0.6 m back, show two calm care-room zones with pale privacy curtains, a bed edge, timber cabinet, chair, soft ceiling light and warm but subtle occupied depth. A shallow integrated planter trough with grasses sits below the windows, and closely spaced vertical timber fins shade one side. Everything must read as layered physical construction, never a printed facade image.

RIGHT PANEL: a front-corner close view through one bay of the triple-height public atrium. Show a real low-iron curtain wall with black pressure caps, separate glass panes, deep sill and roof junction, integrated glulam tree column branching into roof beams, visible CLT bridge/floor edges, transparent balustrades, stair or circulation landing, timber soffit and a warmly occupied lobby set behind the facade. Exterior reflection stays on the glass while interior furniture, lights and structure remain spatially separated. Include a small part of the honey-glulam entry canopy where it joins the atrium frame, proving that it is structurally integrated.

Match the exact materials, proportions and lighting of the supplied hospital. Neutral architectural product photography, crisp microdetail, physically plausible transmission, roughness, clearcoat and depth. No text, people blocking details, opaque blue/black windows, one flat orange room card, mirrored glass, cartoon styling, extra floors, decorative residential balcony, labels or watermark.
